\[

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 1.  A useful series for \(S\)

\[
\frac1{10^{k}-1}= \frac{1}{10^{k}}\frac1{1-10^{-k}}
               = \frac{1}{10^{k}}\sum_{m=0}^{\infty}10^{-km}
               =\sum_{t=1}^{\infty}10^{-kt}.
\]

Thus  

\[
S=\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\sum_{t=1}^{\infty}10^{-kt}
  =\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\tau(n)\,10^{-n},
\]

where \(\tau(n)\) is the number of positive divisors of \(n\).  
(In the double sum each ordered pair \((k,t)\) with \(kt=n\) contributes
\(10^{-n}\); the number of such pairs is exactly \(\tau(n)\).)

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 2.  What we really need

\[
\bigl\lfloor10^{100}S\bigr\rfloor
   =\Bigl\lfloor \sum_{n=1}^{100}\tau(n)10^{100-n}
                +\sum_{n=101}^{\infty}\tau(n)10^{100-n}\Bigr\rfloor .
\]

Write  

\[
X =\sum_{n=1}^{100}\tau(n)10^{100-n},\qquad
B =\sum_{n=101}^{\infty}\tau(n)10^{100-n}.
\]

\(X\) is an integer.  The asked remainder is  

\[
\bigl(X+\lfloor B\rfloor\bigr)\pmod{1000}.
\]

### 3.  Bounding the tail \(B\)

For \(n\ge 101\) we have \(\tau(n)\le 2\sqrt n< 25\).  Hence  

\[
0<B<\sum_{m=1}^{\infty}25\cdot10^{-m}= \frac{25}{9}<3 .
\]

Only the last three powers of 10 survive modulo \(1000\):
\[

\begin{cases}
1 & n=100,\\[2pt]
10 & n=99,\\[2pt]
100 & n=98,\\[2pt]

\end{cases}
\]

Thus

\]
